transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we finalize this plan. My family outreach confirmations from this week show that 38 households lack reliable internet access. Those families will need printed learning packets plus bilingual phone check-ins in Spanish and Somali. I have the confirmation data, but the family-access summary is still being compiled and hasn't been included in the draft plan yet.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical IT issue. District learning-management-system authentication will be offline for scheduled maintenance from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m. tomorrow. I confirmed the maintenance window with the vendor today, but the vendor notice has not yet been attached to the remote-day draft. Since the draft plan schedules instruction through the LMS beginning at 8:00 a.m., we need to change our approach. Instructional files must be distributed by email as downloadable PDFs and made available for printing by 7:30 a.m. This also aligns with the need Ms. Green just raised for printed materials for families without reliable internet access.

This means we cannot send meals by regular bus routes as the draft plan currently assumes. Instead, meals can be made available for on-site pickup at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. The route review results have not yet been added to the operations briefing packet, so Dr. Lee would not have seen this information yet.

transcript.text: I need to flag a nursing coverage issue. The district nurse coverage plan requires a staffed nurse hotline from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. tomorrow for students who need medication or urgent health guidance during remote instruction. The current draft only directs health questions to the usual school voicemail, which would not provide the real-time support students need.
